title: Purity is half of faith
hookLine: purity is half of faith, alhamdulillah fills the scale, prayer is light, charity is proof, patience is brightness (Nawawi 23, Abu Malik al-Ash'ari)
tomorrow: what has God forbidden for Himself, in His own words?

cards: How can washing your hands be half of faith? A sink, some water, the same motions as brushing your teeth. Wash, rinse, done.
It can look like the least spiritual minute of the day. Yet al-Nawawi's twenty-third hadith opens with it: purity is half of faith. Not a tenth.
Not a nice extra. Half. That's the strange detail, and it's only the first of the hadith's strange measurements.
It keeps going, weighing words and prayers like groceries on a scale.

teach.b: From Sahih Muslim, told by Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, in paraphrase: purity is half of faith. Alhamdulillah fills the scale. Subhanallah and alhamdulillah fill what lies between the heavens and the earth.
Prayer is light. Charity is proof. Patience is brightness.
The Qur'an is an argument for you or against you. Everyone goes out in the morning and sells himself, and either frees himself or ruins himself. So, the puzzle: why half?
More than one answer is given. One: purity here means wudu, the washing before prayer, and prayer can't happen without it, so it carries that much weight.
Another: faith clears away what's wrong inside, and purity clears away what's wrong outside, two halves of one cleaning. A third hears purity of the heart, too: letting go of what clings.
The hadith doesn't settle it for you, and a Muslim can hold all three at once: the water on the hands, the prayer it opens, the heart it's meant to clear.
But notice its other units: a word that fills a scale, a prayer that gives off light.

teach.h: WHY HALF? MORE THAN ONE ANSWER.

teach.b: A single alhamdulillah, a word that takes a second, filling a scale. The washing at the sink belongs to that family: an ordinary act the hadith measures big, and one way to start the morning on the freeing side.

how: Muslims make wudu before each prayer: washing the hands, mouth, nose, face and arms, wiping the head, and washing the feet; many begin with 'bismillah' and keep it unhurried.

games.q: what does “purity is half of faith” mean?
o: the washing before prayer, weighing half
a bath required before reading any book

games.q: the hadith's strange measurements — tap the pairs.

s: 'half of faith' means any tidiness counts as half your religion
purity here is wudu, the washing before prayer; some add purity of the heart.
the same hadith says prayer is light and charity is proof
the hadith explains exactly why purity is half
it doesn't; readers give more than one answer.

games.q: your friend jokes that 'purity is half of faith' means cleaning her room is half her religion. what's the better reading?
o: purity here is wudu before prayer, and some add a clean heart.
she's right: any tidiness at all is literally half of faith.
it's only a metaphor, with no link to washing at all.
games.why: readers give several answers, but they start with wudu and the prayer it opens; some add purity of the heart.

practice: If there's water near, wash your hands slowly, the way wudu begins: one hand, then the other, the wrists, between the fingers. Notice the water's temperature, and the sound it makes.
If there isn't, rub your palms together in the same order. Then rest your clean hands in your lap for the sit.

wordCard.voice: Purity is half of faith: at-tuhur, the cleanness wudu brings, the water before the prayer. The hadith's first line, and its biggest measurement.

orig.note: Arabic: purity is half of faith; shatr is the word for half.

carryVoice: Carry this: purity is half, and a sink can be a doorway if you go through it slowly. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: al-Nawawi, al-Arba'in, hadith 23; Sahih Muslim 223 (Abu Malik al-Ash'ari)
